profile.name: Priory
profile.description:
Priory is the leading independent provider of mental healthcare and adult social care in the UK.

We are dedicated to helping people improve their health and wellbeing, not only at our network of hospitals and wellbeing centres, but also on the Priory YouTube channel.

This channel is dedicated to providing 100% free resources for improving your mental health. From short explainers to help you feel more in the known about mental health and addictions, practical self-help walk-throughs to help you boost your wellbeing,  and deep-dive, long-form discussions about the biggest topics in our industry - it is all here for free on the Priory YouTube channel.

Priory is a long-established company, with a prestigious history, with some of the most renowned experts. All of that expertise we're bringing to our YouTube. We create all our content with the help of some of the UK's best psychiatrists, therapists, and other mental health experts.

videos.description: One of the most Googled questions on addiction: “How do I know if I have an addiction?” 💭 In this video, Dee Johnson, Senior Therapist at Priory Hospital Chelmsford, shares the key signs to watch for if you’re concerned about your relationship with alcohol, substances, or behaviors. 🎥 As part of Addiction Awareness Week, this video can help you understand when it might be time to seek support. We understand that seeking help for addiction can feel overwhelming. That’s why we offer a free online Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test (AUDIT) to help you take the first step. Link in bio🔗 #AddictionAwareness #AddictionSupport #LetsTalkAddiction #AAW25

“I think it’s important to say about addiction, because it’s less about the substance or behaviour. It’s more about the pattern of escape that you form.” 💬 Therapist Tess Ridgeway explains how her addiction developed from an underlying need to escape the emotional pain she was experiencing. This clip was take from episode 1 of our new series, Why I Became a Therapist, sharing real stories from the people behind the profession. 🎥 Watch on our YouTube channel [link in bio] 🎧 Or, search Why I Became a Therapist on Spotify or Apple Podcasts #WhyIBecameATherapist #BehindTheTherapy

💬 “I could reach rock bottom and I could carry on digging.” The first episode of Why I Became a Therapist is here! 🎧 For many therapists, the journey into the profession is shaped by their own experiences of struggle, recovery and healing. That’s what this series seeks to explore. In this first episode, Tess Ridgeway Therapist at Priory Hospital Altrincham, shares her honest and inspiring story of addiction, recovery and discovering her own neurodivergence. Also in this episode: ❤️ How Tess became addicted to love, relationships and validation 🆙 What happened when social services helped pick Tess up from her rock bottom 🧠 How late-diagnosis ADHD helped connect the dots of Tess’s addiction 🎥 Watch on our YouTube channel [link in bio] 🎧 Or, search Why I Became a Therapist on Spotify or Apple Podcasts #BehindTheTherapy #WhyIBecameATherapist

Behind every therapist is a story…✍💭 For many, the journey into mental health and addiction support begins with their own experiences - moments of struggle, recovery, understanding and growth. In our new series, Why I Became a Therapist, we’re sharing real stories from the people behind the profession. From experiences of trauma and addiction to neurodiversity and mental health challenges, our therapists open up about what inspired them to support others. 💙 Real stories. Honest conversations. A reminder that lived experience can become a powerful force for helping others find their way. Our six episode series will see a new story release every Tuesday on YouTube, Spotify and Apple Podcasts. 🎥 Watch on our YouTube channel [link in bio] 🎧 Or, search Why I Became a Therapist on Spotify or Apple Podcasts #BehindTheTherapy #WhyIBecameATherapist

🎙️ Six therapists. Six personal journeys. One honest series. Behind the title, the qualifications and training often lies a personal story of struggle, tragedy and recovery. Why I Became a Therapist explores the experiences of six therapists. They share their personal struggles with mental health, addiction or neurodiversity, and how it shaped the work they do today. Watch Why I Became a Therapist, uncovering real stories from the people behind the profession. Starting 15 September, with a new episode every Tuesday on YouTube, Spotify and Apple Podcasts. 🔔 Subscribe to our YouTube channel via the link in bio to be ready for the first episode, or search Why I Became a Therapist on Spotify or Apple Podcasts. 🎧🎥 #WhyIBecameATherapist #BehindTheTherapy

How do you approach someone if you’re worried they might attempt to take their own life? 💙 In this video, suicide attempt survivor and CEO of Chasing the Stigma, Jake Mills, shares advice on how to approach someone you’re concerned about, start the conversation and let them know they’re not alone. You don’t need to have the perfect words. Sometimes, simply asking “Are you okay?” and giving someone the space to talk can be the first step. Watch the full video on YouTube [link in bio] 🔗 #WorldSuicidePreventionDay #SuicidePrevention

You may have heard the phrase ‘committed suicide’. But the word committed is often associated with wrongdoing - we talk about someone ‘committing a crime’ or ‘committing an offence’. Using this language can unintentionally reinforce feelings of shame, blame or judgement around suicide. Instead, try: ➡ ‘Died by suicide’ ➡ 'Took their own life’ ➡ ‘Ended their own life’ Worried about someone who may be feeling suicidal? Read our guide on how to offer support [link in bio] 🔗 #WorldSuicidePreventionDay #SuicidePrevention

Is recovery from addiction about being “cured” – or is it something different? 💭 In this video, Senior Addiction Therapist Dee Johnson explores what recovery really means and why it isn’t always as simple as being “cured”. Over time, repeated behaviours can strengthen neural pathways, making certain thoughts, habits and responses feel automatic. Recovery isn’t necessarily about being “cured”. It can be about understanding these patterns, developing new ways of responding and gradually creating healthier pathways. Watch the full video on YouTube [link in bio] #Addiction #AddictionAwareness #AddictionRecovery

Take an hour to slow down. 🧘‍♀️🎧 Unwind with one hour of 6 Hz theta binaural beats, combined with calming meditation music to create a gentle space for relaxation, mindfulness and quiet time. For the best experience: 🎧 Use headphones to experience the binaural effect 🔈 Keep the volume comfortable and low 💭 Find somewhere quiet where you can sit or lie down 🧘‍♂️ Let the music play while you relax, meditate or simply take a moment for yourself Whether you use it as part of your evening routine, during meditation or simply when you need some uninterrupted quiet time, give yourself permission to pause. Listen to the full hour on YouTube - link in bio 🔗 #Mindfulness #Meditation

Labels can become identities. Negative self-talk can reinforce shame. But changing the language we use can help create space for self-compassion, hope and change. Priory’s Modern Recovery Dictionary explores how reframing the way we talk about addiction - and ourselves - can challenge stigma and support a healthier approach to recovery. ❌ Instead of: Choosing drugs over family ✔ Try: Unable to stop despite the love of their family Because you are not your addiction. You are a person, and recovery is possible. 💙 Discover the Modern Recovery Dictionary and the power of self-talk [link in bio] #Addiction #AddictionAwareness

Why do you think EUPD / BPD still has such a stigma attached to it, especially for women? 💬 People living with borderline personality disorder (BPD), also known as emotionally unstable personality disorder (EUPD) can face assumptions that they are “difficult”, “attention-seeking” or somehow to blame for the challenges they experience. As part of our Ask a Psychiatrist series, Dr David McLaughlan explains how BPD / EUPD can affect how someone experiences emotions, relationship and impulsivity, and these difficulties can be very distressing. Watch the full ‘Ask a Psychiatrist’ video on YouTube [link in bio] 🔗 #BDP #MentalHealthAwareness
